scope: One newly frozen synthetic-profile curriculum and one disjoint final test. No human-model calibration, learning, enjoyment or general-content claim.

learning_assumptions: Author-defined prerequisite: box-goal planning before multi-box goal tracking.
Bot reset on every episode; no learning or human mastery inference.
The 0.25 action-replacement probability is arbitrary synthetic model control, unchanged from v1.
V1 selection and holdout are exploration only. V2 selector uses only newly committed training trials.

explanation: At n=20 one WIN changes observed difficulty by 0.05; selection among 56 candidates on the same seeds magnifies sampling sensitivity.

A holdout shift does not separately identify selection bias and seed noise. The new independent training sample and prespecified 20-seed cohorts describe their scale without retroactively repairing v1.
Common seeds correlate candidates, and deterministic Sokoban makes seed variability a player-execution stream effect rather than new game-state draws.

limitations: The profile parameter 0.25 remains arbitrary and has not been fitted to humans.
Noiseless competent/strong planner controls may saturate, while random may floor; either can leave difficulty bands unidentified for a different population.
Seven retained and three newly authored families are evaluated; this small authored pool does not establish generalization to arbitrary layouts.
The validation set is diagnostic only and was never used for selection; final testing continues even if it fails.
Training Wilson intervals are selection-affected, not post-selection coverage guarantees. Final adjusted intervals are approximate model-sampling diagnostics.
A 256-wide beam is bounded and may miss a better campaign; no exhaustive optimality claim.
Repeated 20-seed cohort differences illustrate finite-sample variability; they do not estimate human variation.
Rest and assessment are authored exposure/runtime checks, not evidence of learning.
